entities.name: Cornelis Evertsen the Elder
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cornelis Evertsen the Elder (died 1666), a distinguished Dutch admiral, emerged as a pivotal naval commander during the tumultuous Anglo-Dutch Wars of the 17th century. Hailing from a prominent Zeeland seafaring family, Evertsen rose through the ranks of the Dutch States Navy, becoming a Vice-Admiral and later Lieutenant-Admiral of Zeeland. His career was defined by fierce engagements against English naval forces, contributing significantly to the Dutch Republic's maritime dominance and its struggle to protect vital trade routes and national sovereignty against a formidable rival. He was a contemporary and peer of other legendary Dutch admirals like Michiel de Ruyter and Maarten Tromp, embodying the era's robust naval traditions.

Evertsen's most notable actions occurred during the Second Anglo-Dutch War (1665-1667). He commanded the Zeeland squadron, playing a crucial role in several major fleet battles. In the momentous Four Days' Battle (June 11-14, 1666), one of the longest naval engagements in history, Evertsen led his ships with valor. On the first day of this colossal clash, while commanding the ship *Walcheren*, he was tragically killed by a cannonball, becoming one of several high-ranking casualties on both sides. His death underscored the brutal realities of naval warfare during this period, where personal leadership on the quarterdeck often meant direct exposure to enemy fire.
